result.rationale: In zoho-bigin/lib/CalendarService.ts, `tokenInfo = await refreshOAuthTokens(async () => await axios.post(...), ...)`. The new refreshOAuthTokens helper (packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/refreshOAuthTokens.ts) returns the raw fetch `Response` when credential sharing is enabled (`return response;` from `fetch(process.env.CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT, ...)`), not an axios object. The subsequent `if (!tokenInfo.data.error)` accesses `.data` on a fetch Response, which is undefined, throwing a TypeError — the same shape mismatch applies to other callers, but the finding correctly cites Zoho Bigin.

judged_text: In sharing mode tokenInfo is a raw fetch Response, so tokenInfo.data is undefined and `if (!tokenInfo.data.error)` throws TypeError. Zoho Bigin calendar operations crash with 'Cannot read properties of undefined (reading error)' on the first token refresh whenever credential sharing is enabled.

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/app-store/zoho-bigin/lib/CalendarService.ts`, the refresh flow was changed to `const tokenInfo = await refreshOAuthTokens(..., "zoho-bigin", credentialId)`. `refreshOAuthTokens` returns a raw `fetch(...)` `Response` object when `APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED && process.env.CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT && userId` is truthy. Because `credentialId` (not `credential.userId`) is passed as the `userId` argument, that condition will likely be true and the function returns a `Response`, not an axios-like object with `.data`. The subsequent code `if (!tokenInfo.data.error)` will then dereference `data` on a `Response`, causing `Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'error')`.
